text:
Naveen: Heads-up — bringing Ophion14b (v2) into int4 canary. Seeing OOMs during long generations when max_new_tokens > 512.
Elaine: repro steps? is this with prefetch enabled?
Naveen: Prefetch=on, batch_size=4, adaptive_window=128, KV cache spikes then OOM. snapshot from node: `oom_kthread: gpu_alloc failed at 7.9GB`
Rob: can you paste the exact deploy config? also which kernel set?
Naveen: config snippet:
```
model: ophion14b-v2
quant: int4
prefetch: true
batching:
  max_batch_size: 8
  target_latency_ms: 120
runtime:
  kernel_profile: auto
  kv_eviction: default
```
Kai: Quick thought — int4 increases per-token compute but reduces weight memory. Frag likely from KV allocations + windowing. Might need KV trim or slot compaction at coldstart.
Elaine: Try lowering max_new_tokens to 384 as a temporary default and set kv_eviction: aggressive for the canary.
Naveen: Ran that: with max_new_tokens=384 OOMs drop ~90% on the canary nodes. But quality regression observed on long-answer evals (bleu-like drops).
bench-bot: Canary bench summary (last run): latency p95 210ms -> 240ms, tokens/s 28, OOMs 2->0, QA F1 -1.8%
Rob: Acceptable trade-off? if production customers need >512 we need a better mitigation not just default change.
Kai: Options: 1) KV trim policy aggressive at tail, 2) windowed batching (shrink batch for long gens), 3) prefetch=false for long sessions, 4) hybrid int4->int8 fallback on memory pressure.
Naveen: I tried KV trim + prefetch backoff: added `kv_eviction: aggressive` and `prefetch_backoff_threshold: 0.7` -> steady for >512 in 1/3 nodes, still hit OOM on older GPU drivers.
Elaine: Can we bisect the regression between int4 quant and kernel selection? try int8 quant with same runtime profile.
Naveen: int8 run attached: no OOMs, latency +18% but QA F1 recovered to baseline. So likely memory layout + int4 runtime path interacting with kernel memory alloc pattern.
Rob: Let's create an experiment matrix and assign owners:
- Naveen: run int4 vs int8 with kv_eviction aggressive/none (4 runs)
- Kai: test prefetch toggles and prefetch_backoff thresholds (3 runs)
- Elaine: run quality evals on long-answer datasets, compute BLEU/F1 deltas
- SRE: reproduce on driver v510 vs v520 (we suspect driver alloc bugs)
Naveen: I'll start matrix now, pushing canary changes to subset (tag: ophion-int4-canary-heap-bisect).
Elaine: Also add a quick difflog to capture KV slot churn: `rviz kv_stats --interval 1s > /tmp/kv-churn.log` in the canary container.
sre-bot: Deploy triggered: ophion-int4-canary-heap-bisect -> 3 nodes (gpux-heavy). Watch logs /alerts.
Rob: If int4 proves flaky we should fallback path: if runtime detects >70% memory pressure during generation, switch to int8 variant automatically. That buys quality and reliability.
Kai: Implementation note: fallback must be seamless for streaming clients — plan: spawn int8 replica and proxy traffic mid-stream with graceful rejoin.
Naveen: Early results: int4 + kv_eviction aggressive + prefetch_backoff 0.6 removed OOMs on 2/3 nodes, driver v520 still 1 OOM. Will attach kv-churn logs in next message.
Elaine: Nice. Once we have logs, schedule a short postmortem/bisect doc with perf numbers and recommended defaults per model. We should avoid global max_new_tokens change — prefer model default.
Naveen: Agreed. Proposing model-default max_new_tokens: 384 for ophion14b-int4, with runtime fallback to int8 above 512.
Rob: +1. Add to rollout checklist: updated canary config, bench regress guard rails, fallback implementation, and customer-impact note.
Kai: I'll draft the rollout playbook.
Naveen: kv-churn excerpt (first 10s):
```
[00:00] slots_in_use: 112
[00:01] slots_in_use: 198
[00:02] slots_in_use: 420 <-- jump after prefetch
[00:03] kv_trim: evicted 120 slots
[00:04] slots_in_use: 320
[00:05] alloc_fail: 1
```
Elaine: That jump looks like aggressive prefetch + int4 allocator fragmentation. Good catch.
bench-bot: Next scheduled bench run in 12m.
Naveen: I'll upload full logs and the experiment matrix CSV to the canary doc after runs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
